title: Portfolio Calibration: Enhancing Visibility of Professional Reasoning
context: An early-career professional whose portfolio primarily showcased aesthetic or technical outputs, lacking the strategic context and decision-making rationale required by senior UK hiring committees.
challenge: Approaching the portfolio as a 'gallery of finished work' rather than a 'diagnostic tool for professional thinking,' failing to address employer concerns regarding problem-solving, stakeholder management, and learning agility.
coaching_pivot: The coaching value focused on the 'Problem-Goal-Result (P-G-R)' narrative structure and 'Logic Mapping.' By converting static screenshots into dynamic case studies, we enabled the client to demonstrate the quality of their professional trade-offs and decisions.
action: Reconstruction of project narrative structures; addition of constraint-based captions; rehearsal of high-fidelity portfolio walkthroughs focused on decision logic.
results: Shift from process-heavy descriptions to outcome-linked professional positioning. Improved ability to articulate reasoning and technical trade-offs during live assessments.
outcome: Advanced to final-round portfolio interviews with specific positive feedback regarding the clarity of their decision-making process.
timeframe: 4 sessions over 5 weeks with integrated asynchronous feedback on scripts and visual structure.
disclaimer: Anonymised composite study for professional illustration.
